evidence.note: Initial plans lay out a clear, dependency-reasonable module ordering (token→lexer→ast→preprocessor→parser→sema→codegen→main), but only at the pass/module level — no feature milestones or explicit completion criteria are defined.

Agent wrote all compiler modules up front in one push before any test ran, then spent ~80 steps just getting a clean build. This is a big-bang approach rather than smallest-viable-slice staging with per-feature done-checks.
Debug phase is organized as reactive bug-by-bug fixing; plans repeatedly say 'identify next most impactful bug pattern' — impact-aware but not a structured feature roadmap tied to test subsets.

Late in the run the agent breaks results down by suite (c_testsuite 54%, wacc 61%, gcc_torture 15%) and decides to 'focus on these standard C tests first' — genuine data-driven prioritization, but arriving only near the end and at triage level, not as a pre-planned milestone hierarchy.
Ending 'Plan' fields remain tactical next-bug lists; no milestone hierarchy with gating criteria ever materialized across the horizon.

reasoning: The agent established a clear pass structure in a reasonable dependency order and loosely tied its work to getting tests passing, with some late impact-based prioritization by suite — matching parts of anchor 5. But it never defined feature-level milestones with concrete test-subset done-signals, and its approach was build-everything-then-debug (big-bang) rather than dependency-ordered smallest-viable slices, keeping it below anchor 5 and well short of the fine-grained, gated milestone structure of anchor 8. This places observed behavior between the 'vague ordering' (3) and 'clear roadmap with loosely-tied milestones' (5) anchors, at a 4.
